# MM-P2-L3-RR01 Maintenance manual - Machining radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01

Scope
This document defines the preventive maintenance actions required to keep the Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) operating within acceptable performance limits for machining operations on forged rings. It covers background, required tools, a stepwise maintenance procedure oriented to safe access and verification, acceptance criteria for restored condition, rationale for each action, examples of typical wear modes, and records to retain. For change history, refer to ECN-2026-018. For routine operational start/stop and safety procedures, consult SOP-P2-L3-01 and SOP-P2-L3-03.

Background and rationale
The radial ring rolling mill is a high-load, high-precision machine subject to cyclical contact stresses and contamination from swarf and coolant. Preventive maintenance focuses on clamping integrity, bearing lubrication, alignment verification, and contamination control. Clamping integrity ensures concentricity and repeatability; bearing lubrication controls friction, heat, and wear. The specified mandrel clamp bolt torque of 470 N·m is the factory-recommended clamping preload required to maintain mandrel positional stability during machining cycles. The main roll bearing lubrication interval of 165 hours is established from bearing supplier life models and machine duty cycles to prevent lubricant starvation and contamination-related failure.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench capable of achieving and verifying the mandrel clamp bolt torque specified as 470 N·m.
- Clean lint-free rags and approved solvent for degreasing mating surfaces.
- Approved bearing grease and dispensing tool as specified in SOP-P2-L3-03.
- Inspection mirror and borescope for internal visual inspection.
- Dial indicator or comparable alignment verification gauge for concentricity checks.
- Torque audit log form and equipment maintenance record forms as defined in SOP-P2-L3-01.

Procedure
Prepare for maintenance:
- Follow lockout/tagout and machine isolation steps in SOP-P2-L3-01 before accessing the machine.
- Clean visible swarf from external surfaces to reduce contamination ingress during maintenance.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque verification:
- Clean bolt heads and mating surfaces using approved solvent and lint-free rags. Rationale: contamination under the bolt head causes inaccurate torque readings and inconsistent clamping force.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, apply the mandrel clamp bolt torque exactly to 470 N·m. Rationale: the specified torque produces the designed clamp preload; under-torque increases risk of mandrel slip, over-torque risks fastener yield. Example: in a recent shop incident, inadequate clamp preload led to concentricity drift and rework; strict torque application prevented recurrence.
- Record applied torque values and any anomalies on the torque audit log form. Include operator initials and equipment serial tag.

Main roll bearing lubrication:
- Inspect bearing housing seals for damage or leakage. Rationale: effective seals maintain lubricant cleanliness and retention.
- Remove access plugs as needed following safe handling guidelines in SOP-P2-L3-03.
- Apply approved lubricant to the main roll bearing following the fill method prescribed in SOP-P2-L3-03. Note the lubrication schedule requirement: main roll bearing lubrication interval for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is 165 hours. Rationale: repeating lubrication at the stated interval prevents lubricant degradation and reduces metal-to-metal contact that accelerates wear.
- Log the lubrication event on the maintenance record, noting the equipment id and lubricant batch/lot per traceability requirements.

Alignment and functional checks:
- Verify mandrel to machine frame concentricity using the alignment gauge. If concentricity exceeds acceptable limits defined in ECN-2026-018, escalate to the engineering team for corrective alignment per ECN-2026-018 instructions.
- Conduct a low-speed functional run per SOP-P2-L3-01 to confirm absence of abnormal vibration or noise. If any abnormal condition is detected, stop and record findings; do not resume production until corrected.

Contamination control and housekeeping:
- Replace or clean coolant screens and filters according to SOP-P2-L3-03. Rationale: coolant contamination contributes to bearing and clamp surface degradation.
- Inspect and clean chip conveyors and collection areas to prevent reintroduction of swarf into critical assemblies.

Acceptance criteria
- Mandrel clamp bolt torque recorded as 470 N·m and verified with a calibrated instrument. Closure condition: torque audit form completed and stored.
- Main roll bearing lubrication event logged with lubricant identification and timestamp, with the interval adherence noted as 165 hours between events. Closure condition: lubrication entry recorded in equipment maintenance record.
- Concentricity within limits specified in ECN-2026-018. Closure condition: alignment verification sheet attached to the maintenance record.
- No abnormal vibration or noise observed during functional verification after maintenance. Closure condition: run test checklist in SOP-P2-L3-01 marked pass.
- Seals intact with no evidence of fresh leakage at bearings or clamp interfaces. Closure condition: visual inspection checklist completed.

Records to keep
- Torque audit log with applied torque values and operator identification. Retain per SOP-P2-L3-01 record retention guidance.
- Bearing lubrication log entries documenting lubricant type and batch, and confirmation that the main roll bearing lubrication interval of 165 hours is observed.
- Alignment verification sheet referencing ECN-2026-018 limits and any corrective actions taken.
- Functional run test checklist from SOP-P2-L3-01 and any deviation reports if issues were found.

Examples and troubleshooting notes
- Example symptom: repeatable concentricity drift observed between shifts. Typical root cause: clamp bolt torque loss from contamination under bolt heads or inadequate torque application. Mitigation: clean bolt interfaces and apply mandrel clamp bolt torque of 470 N·m, then reverify concentricity.
- Example symptom: elevated bearing temperature with increased noise. Typical root cause: lubricant degradation or contamination. Mitigation: inspect seals, replace lubricant, and verify that lubrication events are occurring at the main roll bearing lubrication interval of 165 hours.

References
- ECN-2026-018
- SOP-P2-L3-01
- SOP-P2-L3-03

Revision and change control
All changes to this maintenance manual shall be processed through ECN-2026-018. Record completed maintenance activities on the equipment record for EQ-P2-L3-RR01 and retain records per site document retention practice as described in SOP-P2-L3-01.
